title: Mae Moh Half Marathon 2026 Review: What the 32nd Edition Was Like
seo_title: Mae Moh Half Marathon 2026 Review | Lampang, Thailand
meta_description: Mae Moh Half Marathon review: 3,971 runners on 19 October 2025, a World Athletics label course on fully closed roads past limestone hills and reservoirs.
dek: Northern Thailand's World Athletics-labelled half marathon grew by half in 2025, with nearly 4,000 runners at EGAT Mae Moh in Lampang. Here is what the 32nd edition was like.
verdict: The Mae Moh Half Marathon is a well-established half marathon in Lampang, run around the EGAT power plant and mine at Mae Moh. The 32nd edition, on 19 October 2025, drew 3,971 runners across the 21.1 km, 10 km and 5 km, up by about 50% after the course kept its World Athletics Road Race Label for a second year [1]. The roads were fully closed, and the course passes limestone hills, two reservoirs, the Mae Moh mine and the power plant [1]. Anucha Pada broke the course record in the men's race [1]. If you want a certified half marathon in northern Thailand, it is a good one.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition
paragraphs: The 32nd Mae Moh Half Marathon was held on 19 October 2025 at EGAT Mae Moh in Lampang province, in tribute to Queen Sirikit the Queen Mother [1]. It was organised by the province, the provincial administrative organisation, the Lampang Chamber of Commerce, the Thai Mass Participation Sports Trade Association and EGAT [1].

3,971 runners took part across the 21.1 km half marathon, 10 km and 5 km [1]. EGAT said numbers rose by about 50% after the half-marathon course was certified for a second year by the World Athletics Road Race Label, the first course in northern Thailand to hold it [1].

sections.heading: The Course
paragraphs: The roads were fully closed during the race [1]. The course passes limestone mountains and runs close to the Huai Pet and Mae Kham reservoirs, the Mae Moh mine and the Mae Moh power plant [1].
Because the course is certified, a 21.1 km result from Mae Moh can be used as a qualifying reference for other World Athletics races [1].

sections.heading: The Front of the Race
paragraphs: Anucha Pada broke the course record to win the men's half marathon for the second year running, and Pareeya Sonsem won the women's for the third year running, receiving the Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn trophy [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: If you want a certified half marathon in northern Thailand on closed roads, yes. It is a genuine option for a qualifying time.
The setting is unusual: a working mine and power plant among limestone hills. If that appeals, it is worth the trip to Lampang.
This review is compiled from the co-organiser's report on the 2025 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Mae Moh Half Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: 3,971 runners took part in the 32nd edition on 19 October 2025 at EGAT Mae Moh, Lampang, across the 21.1 km, 10 km and 5 km. That was about 50% more than the year before.

faqs.question: Is the Mae Moh Half Marathon a certified course?
faqs.answer: Yes. The half marathon has a World Athletics Road Race Label, held for a second consecutive year in 2025, and it was the first course in northern Thailand to be certified. Results can be used as a reference for entering other World Athletics races.

faqs.question: What is the Mae Moh Half Marathon course like?
faqs.answer: Fully closed roads through an unusual landscape: limestone hills, the Huai Pet and Mae Kham reservoirs, the Mae Moh mine and the Mae Moh power plant. The men's course record was broken in 2025.
